clue.text: A motley collection of biblical characters

parts.note: Job is the long-suffering patriarch of the Old Testament book named after him
Lot is Abraham's nephew, whose wife was turned to a pillar of salt

explanation.surface: Someone describes a ragtag cast of Old Testament figures.
explanation.walkthrough: One phrase gives two names from the Bible, one after the other.
explanation.definitionFit: A job lot is a mixed batch of goods sold together, hence any assorted bunch.

clue.text: Jill's companion preserves timber and rope for sailors

parts.note: in the nursery rhyme Jack and Jill went up the hill together
to tar wood or cordage is to coat it with pitch to keep it from rotting

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme boy is shown caring for ship's timbers and rigging.
explanation.definitionFit: Jack tar is an old nickname for a seaman of the Royal Navy.

clue.text: Retract support on quiet deal that's been arranged

parts.note: to back someone is to support them
p (piano) is the musical marking for quiet

indicators.note: something arranged has been put into a new order, so the letters of the word deal are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A backer withdraws support from a quiet deal already settled.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's been arranged' gives EDAL; 'on' is a link, the support sitting above the rest in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To backpedal is to withdraw from an earlier position or promise.

clue.text: They take one over water, or round a point

indicators.note: one word placed round another holds it inside, so the word or encloses the letter

parts.note: taken as written
S (south) is one of the compass points

explanation.surface: A ferry description: a boat carries you across, or else round a headland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'round' puts A inside OR to make OAR; S follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Oars propel a rowing boat, carrying a passenger across a lake or river.

clue.text: Partisan assembly produces a candidate

indicators.note: assembling parts means putting them together in a fresh arrangement, so the letters of partisan are rebuilt

explanation.surface: A partisan gathering puts forward its nominee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assembly' rearranges PARTISAN.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspirant is someone seeking a post or honour, a hopeful contender.

clue.text: Evil ruler foundering

parts.note: sin is wickedness, evil-doing
a king is a monarch who rules

explanation.surface: A wicked monarch's reign is collapsing.
explanation.definitionFit: A foundering ship is going down under the water.

clue.text: Disorderly guerrillas making one left turn right

definitions.text: Disorderly guerrillas making one left turn right

indicators.note: disorderly means jumbled, so the letters are shuffled
making one of the letters do something singles out a single letter, not both of the pair
turn here means become, as milk turns sour, so one letter becomes another

explanation.surface: Unruly fighters cause someone to switch from left to right politically.
explanation.walkthrough: Change one L of GUERRILLAS to R, giving GUERRIRLAS, then 'Disorderly' rearranges those letters. Read whole, the clue also describes the answer: irregular, disorderly fighters.
explanation.definitionFit: Irregulars are fighters outside a regular army, such as guerrilla bands.

clue.text: Plea to give one bail, perhaps

indicators.note: perhaps says the letters could be some other arrangement, so they are shuffled

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A lawyer's argument for granting a defendant release on bail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' rearranges I and BAIL.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a defence plea that the accused was elsewhere at the time.

clue.text: In depression, find somewhere to drink

definitions.meaning: a low point, as in the economy or the weather
animals drink from a long open container in a field

explanation.surface: A gloomy person goes looking for a bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is both a hollow or low point and a water container for livestock.

clue.text: Overweight blondes, initially, yearn to get in shape

indicators.note: initially points to the first letter of each of the two words before it

parts.note: to long is to yearn

explanation.surface: Heavy fair-haired people long to become fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'initially' takes O and B from 'Overweight blondes'.
explanation.definitionFit: An oblong is a rectangle, a figure longer than it is wide.

clue.text: Bird killed when in song

parts.note: an English nursery rhyme asks who killed this bird and tells of the sparrow with his bow and arrow

explanation.surface: A songbird shot down mid-song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in song' reads as singing, but it means inside a song: the nursery rhyme.
explanation.definitionFit: The rhyme is about the murder of a male robin, its subject.

clue.text: Money one may charge in Africa

definitions.meaning: an old British slang word for cash
a heavy horned beast of the savanna that charges at threats

explanation.surface: Someone talks about price charges in Africa.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee, given 'Money'; it is a beast stampeding.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhino is old slang for money and short for the African rhinoceros.

clue.text: Record finish of race

definitions.meaning: to ... something is to record it
the ribbon stretched across the finishing line, broken by the winner

explanation.surface: A runner sets a new time at the end of the race.
explanation.definitionFit: Tape is both a recording medium and the strip broken at the finishing line.

clue.text: Four-cornered circle

parts.note: a paradox: the square arena where fighters meet is still called by a word for a circle

explanation.surface: An impossible geometric figure: a circle with corners.
explanation.definitionFit: A boxing ring is square, with four corners, yet is called a ring.

clue.text: Escape route George automatically takes

parts.note: flight is fleeing, escape
a path is a route

explanation.surface: Someone named George always follows the same getaway road.
explanation.walkthrough: 'George' is pilots' slang for the autopilot, which follows the programmed course automatically.
explanation.definitionFit: A plane's autopilot steers it along a set course through the air.

clue.text: Revolutionary air followed by early motorists

definitions.meaning: a socialist anthem, the song of the British Labour movement
under the 1865 British Locomotive Act a man carrying a warning banner walked ahead of motor vehicles

explanation.surface: A rebel song is played behind the first car drivers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'followed' reads as coming after, but the man with the flag walked in front and motorists followed him.
explanation.definitionFit: The Red Flag is the Labour anthem; a red flag also warned of early cars.

clue.text: Illegal wayfarers seen around part of Ireland

indicators.note: the letters are seen in the run of the clue words, carried across the two words

explanation.surface: Unlawful travellers spotted in an Irish county.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seen' signals letters within 'Illegal wayfarers'; 'around' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Galway is a county and city on Ireland's west coast.

clue.text: Fear arrest

definitions.meaning: to dread or anticipate with anxiety
to seize and take into custody

explanation.surface: A suspect dreads being taken in by police.
explanation.definitionFit: Apprehend means both to anticipate with dread and to seize a suspect.

clue.text: It will contain a fire

parts.note: contain means holding flames back, not holding a fire inside: a fireproof mineral fibre

explanation.surface: A fireplace or grate that holds a fire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'contain' suggests a grate holding a fire; it means keeping a blaze from spreading.
explanation.definitionFit: This mineral fibre was used in fireproof materials because it does not burn.

clue.text: Get off for a match

definitions.meaning: to step down from a vehicle or horse
a request for a light, something to ignite with

explanation.surface: Someone asks a passenger to dismount for a game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'match' looks like a game but is a lit stick; split the answer as two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Alight means to dismount; a light is a flame, as a match provides.

clue.text: One may take it to avoid it

definitions.text: One may take it to avoid it

parts.words: One may take it to avoid it
parts.note: a word meaning both care or effort and difficulty: you take pains to keep out of strife

explanation.surface: A paradoxical remark about taking something in order to avoid it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taking trouble means making an effort; avoiding trouble means escaping difficulty.

clue.text: So a returning rugby player is accepted as fit

parts.note: a prop is a front-row forward in rugby

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the word so is read backwards

explanation.surface: A rugby forward who comes back is accepted as fit to play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives OS, which ends the answer; 'is accepted as' is a link phrase, and 'fit' means suitable, not healthy.
explanation.definitionFit: Apropos means pertinent or appropriate, apt to the occasion.

clue.text: Maintain a lock up

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair

explanation.surface: An instruction to keep a door locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns TRESS to SSERT.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert is to maintain or insist that something is true.

clue.text: Secure in boat in storm

indicators.note: a storm throws things about, so the letters are tossed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is safe aboard a boat during a storm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'storm' makes OBTA; the first 'in' is a link, the second is kept as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: To secure something is to get hold of or acquire it.

clue.text: Green boots could get you the bird

indicators.note: the letters could produce something different when rearranged, so they are shuffled

explanation.surface: Wearing wellingtons in a hide is how a birdwatcher spots their quarry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could get you' rearranges GREEN BOOTS.
explanation.definitionFit: The brent goose is a small dark goose that winters on coasts.

clue.text: One may slip and fall into it

definitions.text: One may slip and fall into it

parts.words: One may slip and fall into it
parts.note: slip means a blunder, and one falls into a mistake rather than a hole

explanation.surface: Someone loses their footing and tumbles into a ditch.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip is a mistake, and people are said to fall into a blunder.

clue.text: We hear top player is to step down

indicators.note: what we hear is a word said aloud, which sounds like the one entered

parts.note: a seed is a top-ranked player in a tennis tournament

explanation.surface: A tournament favourite is reportedly about to retire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is to' is a link before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede is to give up or yield a position to another.

clue.text: Trees spring up round South

indicators.note: the reversed word goes round the letter for south, holding it inside
in a down clue up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a spa is a mineral spring

explanation.surface: Trees grow upward around a southern spring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SPA to APS; 'round' places it around S.
explanation.definitionFit: Asp is an old poetic word for the aspen tree.

clue.text: Arterial way of vital importance

parts.note: arterial way sounds like a trunk road, but it is the body's main blood vessel

explanation.surface: A major highway described as essential.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arterial way' suggests a main road; vital also hints at life.
explanation.definitionFit: The aorta is the main artery carrying blood from the heart.

clue.text: Chinese soup ingredient often includes eggs

definitions.meaning: swiftlet saliva nests are a delicacy used in a Chinese soup
a home built by a bird usually holds eggs

explanation.surface: A Chinese soup recipe that often adds eggs.
explanation.definitionFit: A bird's nest is both a costly Chinese soup ingredient and where eggs are laid.

clue.text: Could be another's fishing ground

indicators.note: could be says the letters might form another word, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A fishing area that might belong to someone else.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Could be' rearranges ANOTHERS, the S of the possessive included.
explanation.definitionFit: The North Sea is a major fishing area between Britain and Scandinavia.

clue.text: Remarks we're not sup posed to hear when the team comes in

definitions.text: Remarks we're not sup posed to hear

indicators.note: one word comes in another when placed inside it

parts.note: as means when, as in as I left
a side is a team

explanation.surface: Things said off-stage while the players run on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' for AS is the sense in 'as the sun set'; the printed clue splits 'supposed' in two.
explanation.definitionFit: On stage, an actor's aside is spoken to the audience, unheard by other characters.
